Hi Sofia / Steven —

Thanks again for the conversation today — great to learn more about how Acme Health is planning to use Redwood for in-product clinical summarization and triage routing. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned for the POC: 

- High-level success criteria (from our call):
  • 90%+ precision on triage label classification for high-severity cases (prod-critical)
  • Summaries under 120 tokens with >85% clinician-rated accuracy on a 5-point Likert
  • End-to-end latency for summary generation < 800ms p50 for typical encounter length

- What we need from you to run the eval:
  1) Prompt set: representative user prompts and system instructions (~200–500 prompts ideally)
  2) Conversation logs: 1,000–2,000 de-identified chat/encounter records (CSV or JSONL) with a sample set of gold labels for triage and a small set of human-rated summaries for eval (50–100).
  3) Optional: top 10–20 failure cases or examples you care most about so we can prioritize.

- Privacy/format notes: Please remove or hash direct patient identifiers before sending (we can accept a mapping key under an NDA if necessary). If you need specific redaction guidance, Aditya can provide a script.

- Timeline (proposed):
  • Receive data & prompts by EOD Thu, 3 Jun 2027
  • Initial eval run + summary of results by Tue, 9 Jun 2027
  • Checkpoint call to review findings Wed, 11 Jun 2027 (30–45 min)

- Ownership:
  • Acme: deliver prompt set + de-identified logs (Sofia / Steven)
  • Redwood: onboarding + run evals (Marissa coordinating; Aditya technical lead; Dev to provision cluster if needed)

Attachments: I’ve included a draft POC eval plan (redwood_poc-eval-plan_v2.docx) for your review — it lists required fields and an example CSV schema.

If that timeline works, please reply with the files or a confirmation of the expected delivery date. Happy to adjust if you need more time.

Best,

Thanks Marissa / Sofia — quick technical clarifications from our side so the eval runs smoothly: 

1) File formats: CSV or JSONL are both fine. For CSV please include a header row and use UTF-8. For JSONL, one record per line.
2) Required fields: record_id, timestamp, clinician_role, encounter_text, triage_label (if available), ground_truth_summary (optional but highly useful). The sample schema is in the doc Marissa attached.
3) Size & sampling: 1,000 records is sufficient for an initial run; 2,000 preferred for more stable metrics. If you can provide a stratified sample (by specialty / severity) that will help interpret results.
4) Redaction/PII: Hashing names and MRNs is fine. For free-text PHI, our automated scrubber can help but we need a small sample (10–20 records) with identifiers to validate. If you prefer not to share mappings, we’ll run the scrubber and send a report describing removed tokens.
4) Metrics we’ll compute: precision/recall/F1 for triage labels, ROUGE and simple semantic similarity for summaries, and latency distribution by token length. If you have custom metrics you want included, please share.

One ask: please include a short doc (1–2 paragraphs) describing the expected user flows where these prompts are used (e.g., clinician open note flow, nurse triage flow). That helps us pick prompt templates that match production behavior.

Estimate: once we have the files, initial eval will take ~48–72 hours to run end-to-end (data ingestion, model run, metric computation), assuming no provisioning delays. If we need burst GPUs we’ll flag Dev to provision dedicated capacity.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min sync if that helps align formats.

—Aditya
